citations.narrative:
Toys placed inside the primary enclosure for one common marmoset are not being maintained in a way that protects the
animal from injury. On the floor of the enclosure, there are multiple piles of stuffing from inside of a stuffed animal toy.
Damaged items can allow nonhuman primates access to inappropriate materials which can lead to illness or injury from
ingestion. Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained so that they protect the nonhuman primates from
injury.
To be corrected by October 19, 2026.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The licensee is not spot cleaning two indoor marmoset enclosures daily.
In an indoor enclosure housing one common marmoset and an indoor enclosure housing one common marmoset and one
black-tufted marmoset, there is an accumulation of excreta and food waste on the floor and surfaces. When the inspector
asked when the last time the enclosure had been cleaned, the licensee stated that it had been about a week.
Failure to clean as often as necessary can lead to the buildup of feces, secretions, food waste, and debris which may
attract insects or vermin, and increase the risk of disease transmission. Excreta and food waste must be removed from
inside each indoor primary enclosure daily and from underneath them as often as necessary to prevent an excessive
accumulation of feces and food waste, to prevent the nonhuman primates from becoming soiled, and to reduce disease
hazards, insects, pests, and odors.
To be corrected by October 19, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
